summary:
Farm Profile & Goals: Configured for District A with Loam soil and Low water availability during the Kharif season. It targets a 50% max risk tolerance and a minimum profit floor of ₹10,000.  
​Weather & Forecast: The 7-day forecast predicts a cumulative 65.0 mm of rainfall with peaks on Oct 19, 24, and 25. It warns of potential surface runoff, waterlogging, and high fungal pathogen risk due to 94% humidity.  
​NASA POWER Integration: Satellite parameters (temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, solar irradiance, soil wetness, and wind speed) supplement ground telemetry to refine evapotranspiration models, crop maturity calculations, and yield forecasts.  
​Action Plan: Farmers should balance drainage with moisture retention, use mulch to manage high thermal stress, apply preventative fungicides, and input their exact acreage and capital budget into the Smart Crop Advisor to select resilient Kharif crops.
details: ​1. Farm Configuration & Economic Filters (Smart Crop Advisor) ​Location & Soil: The farm is set in District A on Loam soil, which offers balanced drainage, nutrient retention, and broad crop compatibility. ​Resource Constraints: Operates under a "Low" water availability classification (restricting water-intensive crops) during the Kharif growing season. ​Financial & Risk Parameters: Configured with a maximum risk tolerance of 50% to filter out high yield/price volatility, and enforces a minimum net profit expectation floor of ₹10,000. ​Pending Inputs: The user still needs to input their exact farm size in hectares and their total investment budget into the sidebar. ​2. Local Meteorology & 7-Day Forecast (District A) ​Reference Observation (Oct 19, 2025): Recorded ambient temperatures ranged from 22^{\circ}C to 31^{\circ}C (9^{\circ}C diurnal spread) alongside 94% relative humidity, overcast skies, and 18.2 mm of daily rainfall. ​7-Day Precipitation & Temperature Trend: ​The week accumulates 65.0 mm of rainfall, featuring distinct wet bursts on Oct 19 (18.2 mm), Oct 24 (14.4 mm), and Oct 25 (17.1 mm). ​Mid-week days (Oct 20–22) transition to clear/sunny conditions with daytime highs peaking up to 35^{\circ}C. ​Operational Weather Advisories: ​Heavy Rainfall Warning: Surface runoff and waterlogging are likely on loam soils during peak events, requiring verified field drainage channels. ​Fungal Pathogen Risk: Prolonged canopy wetness combined with warm daytime highs (29^{\circ}C-35^{\circ}C) creates high vulnerability for foliar fungal outbreaks. ​3. NASA POWER Satellite Agroclimatology Integration ​The report integrates 0.5^{\circ} \times 0.5^{\circ} satellite and reanalysis data from NASA POWER (GMAO MERRA-2 and GPM IMERG) to bridge gaps in ground station telemetry: ​T2M_MAX / T2M_MIN: Validates thermal ranges (18^{\circ}C-35^{\circ}C) and computes Growing Degree Days (GDD) for Kharif crop maturity. ​PRECTOTCORR: Supplies bias-corrected total precipitation to evaluate whether low water availability requires supplemental irrigation. ​RH2M: Benchmarks the 94% humidity spike against seasonal norms to calibrate disease alerts. ​ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN: Quantifies photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) during sunny vs. cloudy intervals to refine yield forecasts. ​GWETTOP / GWETROOT: Tracks 0–5 cm and 0–100 cm soil wetness in loam soil between rainfall pulses. ​WS2M: Measures 2-meter wind speed to feed into FAO-56 Penman-Monteith reference evapotranspiration (ET_0) calculations. ​4. Integrated Agronomic Synthesis & Action Matrix ​Moisture vs. Drainage: Construct perimeter bunds or farm ponds to capture surplus runoff from the 65.0 mm weekly rainfall while preventing acute waterlogging. ​Thermal Stress & ET_0 Management: High mid-week temperatures (34^{\circ}C-35^{\circ}C) under clear skies increase evapotranspiration; retaining crop residue mulch helps preserve surface soil moisture. ​Proactive Disease Control: Preventative biological or low-cost fungicide applications should be prioritized within the budget to protect the ₹10,000 minimum net profit threshold against high humidity risks. ​Model Execution Readiness: Entering precise farm acreage and capital budget into the application triggers machine-learning rankings for drought-resilient Kharif crops (like millets, pulses, or oilseeds) suited for loam soils.
